problem: Existing audio-visual navigation tasks (AudioGoal, SemanticAudioGoal, FFO) assume zero-shot single-scene search for a sound source and do not require deciding whether the sound indicates a real emergency. They also do not use prior exploration or knowledge of where people usually are in a home.
motivation: Accidental home deaths (falls, fires) exceed 128k per year in the US, and a home robot cannot be in every room, so audio is a natural trigger for a fast response. The robot must find the source across multiple rooms from short aperiodic sounds and avoid false alarms (e.g. a fallen box vs a fallen person).
key_idea: Represent moving agents in a dynamic scene graph via probabilistic edges (P-DSG, a human-activity heatmap), and fuse these with audio label and direction by Bayesian inference over rooms, then verify the emergency with a VLM.
insight: Both inference terms matter: removing P(a_dir|r) or P(a_l|r) drops falls AG SR from 0.75 to 0.58 and raises EDFNR from 0.20 to 0.47/0.45, with direction hurting SPL more. The human-activity prior is also critical: adding noise to the heatmap (sigma 1.0) degrades falls AG SR to 0.62 and EDFNR to 0.43, close to the no-prior ablation. Periodic audio raises falls AG SR to 0.90, so information from the sound is the bottleneck. End-to-end RL (PPO) and FFO fail in the multi-room, aperiodic setting.
method: HomeEmergency dataset (ThreeDWorld): 36 multi-room homes, fall and fire scenarios, positive and negative (distractor) samples, 1152 episodes. Fall placement uses HOMER activity schedules; audio is propagated by the simulator; 500-step limit.

P-DSG mapping: 3-layer scene graph (rooms, places, objects) where object nodes are static (o_o) or dynamic agents (o_ag). Agent nodes carry probabilistic edges to rooms/places, set from a routine/heatmap and lowered when a room is seen to be empty.

Audio perception: Whisper-AT labels 4 s overlapping windows (527 classes). Emergency-related labels (thud, alarm) trigger localization, and the audio direction a_dir is used (pseudo-truth direction of the nearest room opening in simulation; mic-array max amplitude in the real world).

Bayesian inference: P(r|a) ∝ P(r)·P(a_l|r)·P(a_dir|r). P(a_l|r) is P(Ag|r) from agent edges for falls, or LLM-derived fire-likelihood of objects summed per room for fires. P(a_dir|r) is a step function (0.99/0.01) on whether the path to the room agrees with the direction.

Navigation and re-planning: go to the highest-probability room, update the prior P(r) when no emergency is seen so other rooms get searched, and recompute on new audio. In negative episodes the agent clears the whole home.

Emergency identification: LLaVA 1.6 is prompted with egocentric RGB plus a 360° view on room entry, answering yes/no with reasoning about fallen users or fire; the agent stops only when an emergency is detected.

setting.backbone: Whisper-AT (frozen) + LLaVA 1.6 (frozen) + LLM for object traits + Bayesian room inference on P-DSG
setting.training_data: none (training-free modular method; baselines FFO and PPO are trained in TDW)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D, microphone audio (label + direction), plus prior 2D occupancy map, 2D room map and noisy human-activity heatmap
setting.action_space: discrete: turn 15° left/right, forward 0.15 m, collect audio (Magnebot); room-level goals then path planning
setting.privileged: Pseudo-ground-truth audio direction (nearest room-opening boundary on the shortest path) in simulation; prior exploration providing occupancy map, room map, and a noisy HOMER-based human activity heatmap; oracle stopping for AG SR

numbers.eval_set_note: 1152 episodes split evenly between falls/fires and positive/negative; falls half reported here

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own HomeEmergency dataset, not a standard benchmark. Only the falls/fires class-level tables are reported, with no overall aggregate. Noise ablation (sigma 0.05/0.15/1.0) rows are omitted.
results: On falls the method reaches AG SR 0.75, SPL 0.63 and EDFNR 0.20, versus the strongest baseline DF at 0.57/0.52/0.53. On fires it reaches AG SR 0.86, SPL 0.73 and EDFNR 0.31 vs DF at 0.72/0.67/0.47, while FFO and PPO are at or below 0.17 SR. The real-robot demo gives SR 0.83 and EDFNR 0.10 vs DF at 0.60.
limitations: Assumes an existing human-activity heatmap, which raises privacy concerns
No significant background noise in simulation or real tests, and audio direction is pseudo-ground truth in simulation
Only falls and fires are covered, and the real-world test is small (30 trials, simplified apartments)
